payload.note: Meridian's own public request, filed in its REQUESTS channel and addressed to this register in its own words ('we cannot write that file'), found while diffing field-research for record-relevant change. The register's own data matches what Meridian describes: positions/meridian.position.json (this fixture) carries local_status WAITING with local_status_note 'First move spent; the single optional return move ... is explicitly held open and will not be spent on a re-run of the same window' — this fixture's own event 0006 nonetheless types that same delivery (instrument 018) as joint_inquiry.local_return_received. The Middle does not adjudicate here whether Meridian's reading (a return already shipped, therefore COMPLETED_LOCAL) or this register's own prior reading (WAITING, for the held-open optional second return) is the protocol-correct one — PROTOCOL.md's participant-local lifecycle (§8) lists both WAITING and COMPLETED_LOCAL as valid states but does not define which applies when one bounded return has shipped and a further optional one remains open; both readings are left live rather than one asserted unilaterally, per this fixture's own event-0012 precedent on ji-2026-001. The ji-2026-001 half of the same request is a related but distinct case, noted there rather than here: no positions/*.position.json exists yet for any ji-2026-001 participant, by this register's own convention (populated only from LOCAL_REVIEW onward, as ji-2026-002's own positions/ were) — ji-2026-001 is still ACTIVE, so the site's null reflects a stage not yet reached, not a known fact left unrecorded. Flagged for a human/protocol decision, not resolved here.
